Internally, the MC7 has impressive stats. Its Owl-Eye Optical sensor goes all the way up to a max DPI of 30,000, and the polling rate of 8,000 Hz is competitive-level. That's so high, in fact, that the average person won't even see the benefit of it.

And the elephant in the room here: the 2.25-inch colour display is touch-sensitive too, which means you can flick through a couple of different screens depending on your use case. We have seen screens on gaming mice before, like the Cooler Master MM830 and SteelSeries Rival 710 (neither of which are touch screens), but as far as I can tell, the MC7 is the largest on a modern gaming mouse from a reputable brand. That makes it an oddity at the least.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/w9Dy3EoWsX6eaDaEVRrCna-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/ezp7xv5zboramJmffMpGKc-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/PuV3MAou88jBtv7GDuPE4c-1920-80.jpg

But that's not all the MC7 has going for it. The 4D scroll wheel means you can go up, down, left and right on a page with just the wheel, and you have extra buttons here, too. You have one at the bottom of the thumb rest, another next to the mouse wheel, plus two on the left-hand side, as well as your standard clicks.

It's a wireless mouse, so it comes with a 2.4 GHz receiver, and it also has hot-swappable batteries. The battery charger has a spare USB Type-A port, which means your charger can also be the receiver. This is a sweet system, which makes the MC7 feel like it has infinite battery (as long as you are willing to spend twenty seconds swapping the battery every 10 or so hours).
Performance

The Owl-Eye sensor is great. It's consistent and smooth, and never posed any problems in any of the games I threw this mouse at. For everyday gaming, I don't have any complaints about how its internals performed. It's a slightly customised version of the PixArt PAW3950 sensor, and will be familiar to anyone who's used the Razer Deathadder V3 Pro, which previously had the exclusive use of PixArt's 30K sensor.

The mouse clicks are a tad loud for my liking, but they're plenty snappy. This bad boy is fitted with Titan Optical switches, and they are perfect under my fingertips. I have yet to hit a single double-click and find them to be very responsive.

However, the biggest problem with performance is how the MC7's weight is balanced and how it feels under the palms. At 135 g grams, it's a fairly heavy mouse (more so than the recent Naga V3 Pro and its mountain of buttons), but this wouldn't be too big of a problem if it could balance that weight in a comfortable way.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/vD6bxaDXoWTpg2Ra9AeQoA-1920-80.png
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/xtCz82ceDbkEFLdTqpTAnA-1920-80.png
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Khx2BrpmWBjjVJBJZT2auA-1920-80.png

However, it feels clunky, and even has a slight rattle at high speeds. This all contributes to a mouse that feels a little lacking in competitive play, even though it's got the internal chops to handle everything on paper.

In use, the screen is rather peculiar. Via the Turtle Beach Swarm II software, you can flit between a few screens, which you customise with your own controls, and they are fairly snappy and responsive. However, having to arch my fingers to actually click on the screen means it's not intended for quick play. That makes it better as a micro function, or a way of displaying battery (but the device's lighting can already indicate battery life and DPI setting). It can display things like health and ammo in Counter-Strike 2, but its viewing angles are pretty poor, meaning it doesn't offer much of a tactical advantage.
Battery Life

The MC7 comes with two 1000 mAh batteries, both of which are hot-swappable. They connect to a charger (which also has a USB port for your 2.4 GHz connector), and this means you technically only need one USB to do everything for your mouse. It's a great system.

To swap the batteries out, you simply take off a compartment where your palm rests, pull the battery out and put a new one in. The MC7's onboard battery is just big enough that I've never noticed the device dying while I'm changing batteries. It's pretty sweet, and with a little practice, it can be swapped in seconds. It's not quite as quick to swap as the Glorious Model O Eternal , with its open battery system, but it is a bit tidier.

Working on my PC every day, then gaming most nights, I found myself swapping out the battery every few days at 1,000 Hz polling, which is perfectly solid given how convenient swapping the batteries is.

content.v: Preorders are opening up for physical editions of Nightdive's Thief Remaster , and at the high end, the studio is offering an homage to Thief's iconic original PC big box packaging in that shape we all know and love, the trapezoid. The only problem? Nightdive and partner Clear River Games are only offering it for Switch/Switch 2 and PS5.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/qQcMbNpDMFnCkQrpD5HPpn-1920-80.png

It doesn't really, at least not as much as war and death and politics or whatever. But Thief's original '90s big box edition came in a jaunty little trapezoidal box unlike anything else on the market. It remains a visually striking, highly sought-after collector's item. It's fun, it's memorable, and it's a piece of PC gaming history. I've had to settle for my version of Thief Gold that came in a plain Jane regular box as a reissue.

It's not super surprising that Night Dive and Clear River eschewed a PC version of this physical release⁠—that's fairly common these days, even in boutique indie special editions. I had a similar "we're so back, it's so over" reaction when I saw that indie RPG heater Dread Delusion's limited physical edition had skipped PC.

But the hurt feels new all over again when it's a PC gaming icon like Thief, and a PC gaming phenomenon like the big box. I would have dropped a fat hundo on a physical PC version of Thief Remastered in a heartbeat⁠—it's why I live in an apartment and not a house.

And studios still do come out with physical editions of their PC games: My Baldur's Gate 3 big box has pride of place in my office. All told, it's just a slight bummer and frustration trying to drag down one of my most anticipated games. I'm still going to play the hell out of it when it comes out on December 3, though.

I'm rooting for GOG's proposal to bring back the big box . The company seems to be considering a boutique service where you can purchase physical versions of the games in your library, which sounds pretty rad to me.

items.summary: Developer S-Game's action-RPG Phantom Blade Zero launched on October 29 and had a massive start across PC and

content.v: Developer S-Game's action-RPG Phantom Blade Zero launched on October 29 and had a massive start across PC and PS5.
The game sold more than 4 million copies over its first 72 hours. That works out to 926 units sold per minute or about 15.4 per second over the first three days.
"Thank you everyone from the bottom of our hearts for all the love and support," the studio said in a social media post.
The 4 million figure counts copies sold across both PC and PS5--the game is not available on Xbox. The game reached a record of 833,921 peak concurrent users on Steam on November 1.
The game's developer is based in China, and the majority of preorders for the game came from China, Taiwan, and Hong Kong.

Phantom Blade Zero's sales out of the gate are strong, but do not come close to another hit game from the Chinese game developer scene, Black Myth: Wukong. That game sold 10 million copies over its first three days . The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, meanwhile, sold 10 million copies in three days as well.
If you’re looking to get started, you can check out our Phantom Blade Zero guides hub for many walkthroughs on increasing your power and finding rare items.
“S-Game’s Wuxia-inspired combat puts you in the middle of a Chinese action movie,” Richard Wakeling wrote in GameSpot’s Phantom Blade Zero review .

items.summary: World of Warcraft Forever is just a few days away, and Blizzard has confirmed the global release times and pre

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/09/15/wowoo-1789495563832.png
World of Warcraft Forever is just a few days away, and Blizzard has confirmed the global release times and preload details.

WoW Forever launches on November 4, and has a global release scheduled, which means everyone will be able to start playing at the same time, no matter where they are. This is super important in an MMO like WoW, because it means that one region isn't able to get significantly further ahead than any other.
World of Warcraft Forever Global Release Times

Because World of Warcraft Forever has a global release, all you really have to do is look at its official release time of 3pm PST and convert that to your own timezone. However, because of the nature of a global release, depending on where you are in the world, the game will either be launching on November 4 or on November 5.
World of Warcraft Forever Preload Details

World of Warcraft Forever is available to preload now. Simply open or download the Battle.net launcher, then WoW Forever should show up in the 'Favorites' bar by default. If it doesn't, go to 'Games' and then search for 'World of Warcraft.' Then, click the WoW icon, go to 'game version' and ensure 'WoW Forever' is selected, and then hit the big blue 'Install' button.
Once it's downloaded you'll be good to log in when the servers go live on November 4 at 3pm PST.
How Much Space Will You Need For World of Warcraft Forever?

According to Blizzard's system requirements, World of Warcraft Forever will need at least 128GB of available space, but I'd actually reserve a bit extra. Just like any version of WoW, there are going to be hundreds of mods available from day one, and unless you're looking to play the game entirely with the default UI, you're going to want to make sure you have some space for add-ons. I'd recommend having at least 150GB reserved for Forever, just in case. Note, as well, that Blizzard specifically calls out an SSD, rather than a harddrive.

According to Art Director Aya Shida, the team was consciously fighting a battle between making the game more realistic with the improved power of the Switch 2, and retaining the spirit of the original — a somewhat dark world, filled with weird characters. She therefore relied on phrases like “a puppet-show feel” and “the analogue feel of practical effects films” during development to reflect the goal: "both create a convincing sense that the characters truly exist within their respective fantasy worlds".

The Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is set to release this Thursday, November 5. The first batch of physical copies of the game includes a textured foil cover – but these will only be available while supplies last.

That day has come at Amazon ; the retailer sold through its supply of textured-foil-cover copies over the weekend. Thankfully, if you haven’t preordered it yet and you want a copy with a reflective cover, you can still preorder it at a few retailers ( see it at Walmart ).
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2) with Foil Cover

While the foil cover is available at several retailers, Walmart is the only one offering a $10 preorder discount. So if you want a foil cover edition of the game, and you want to save $10, you should absolutely preorder it from Walmart before it’s gone. I’d do it ASAP if I were you.
The textured foil on the cover creates a sparkling reflection effect when you rotate the game case in the light. You can see what it looks like up close in Nintendo's Instagram post below.

Amazon’s listing for the Ocarina of Time remake has a note saying it will be “available again starting Nov. 5,” but I’m fairly certain the new stock will have a standard, non-textured, non-foil cover.

Nintendo is going all out on the Ocarina of Time remake by releasing a host of Zelda-themed consoles and accessories alongside it (see our preorder guide for full details). But as these things tend to do, nearly all of the additional items sold out long ago. Some will be available again at certain retailers on November 5 – including at Best Buy’s midnight launch for the game – so not all hope is lost if you haven’t been able to lock in a preorder.

items.title: 白手起家的百万富翁表示购买 GTA 6 可以节省 5,000 美元
items.summary: British self-made millionaire, entrepreneur, and social media educator Mark Tilbury put out a video giving the

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/11/02/gta-6-1793635899315.png

British self-made millionaire, entrepreneur, and social media educator Mark Tilbury put out a video giving the most sound financial advice of 2026: buy GTA 6 . According to him, it’ll save you a big chunk of change.

“GTA 6 costs $99.99,” he said, going straight for the more expensive Ultimate Edition rather than the $80 standard edition (perhaps he, like many others, consider the Ultimate Edition and its extra contents to be the default version). “If it takes you 80 hours to complete, that’s $1.25 per hour of fun. But once you add in side missions and explore the map, it’s down to 50 cents an hour.

“Now let’s say you play for four hours every evening, that’s 50 nights of entertainment. Compare that to going out, where you could easily spend $100 in a single night. That’s why buying GTA 6 actually saves you $5,000.”

Obviously the video is tongue-in-cheek and not actual financial advice (who’s going out 50 nights in a row and spending $100 a pop?). But it’s actually a fair point on the value proposition of the game. An investment in your time, if you will.

That’s why publishers are reportedly hoping GTA 6 sets a new precedent on game pricing — other companies will struggle to compete with its size and scale. It seems like the kind of game you could play for hundreds of hours, and that’s before GTA Online even comes into the equation.
“I’m a 40yo gamer, don't drink much, don't smoke, don't do drugs or go out with friends,” said one commenter. “This is how I explain me gaming to people.”
“Straight to mum,” said another. “Rockstar paid a billion dollars for it, so it’s a steal at the end of the day,” said another mathematician.
Tilbury is a businessman best known for his videos on frugal living. Despite being a millionaire, he reuses old cups, flies economy, wears the same rotation of clothes, and avoids luxury hotels.

We’ve got plenty more on GTA 6 while you wait for its November 19 release date, including an unlikely gameplay reveal in the latest episode of South Park , how GTA 6 named one of its biggest mechanics after a beloved GTA 4 meme , and how GTA 6's map will open up relatively early and let you explore freely .

items.title: GTA 6 购买指南：为贴纸冲击做好准备
items.summary: Rockstar's GTA 6 finally releases on November 19, and if you're looking to play the game, you'll also need a c

content.v: Rockstar's GTA 6 finally releases on November 19, and if you're looking to play the game, you'll also need a console--and those are more expensive than ever. Here's a quick buying guide to help you understand what you need and how much the items will cost.
A console

First, you'll need a PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X|S console. The least expensive option for buying a new system outright is the Xbox Series S, which costs $500. Unfortunately, that's $200 more expensive than the system cost at launch in 2020--there are a number macroeconomic and AI factors that drove prices up significantly .

A new Xbox Series X, meanwhile, costs $750 for a system with no disc drive, or $800 for a console with a disc drive. GTA 6 is not available on a disc, but having a disc drive may still be important to you for other games and media like DVDs and Blu-rays.

Switching to PlayStation, the least expensive system on Sony's side is the $600 digital edition, scaling up to $900 for a PS5 Pro (with a disc drive). PS5 Pro, as the most powerful of these options, is likely to provide the best experience from a technical and graphical standpoint, although the gameplay itself should be identical across all platforms.

These are all prices for brand-new units, but Sony offers certified refurbished PS5 consoles starting at $500. A certified refurbished Xbox Series S, meanwhile, goes for $400. These are the prices from Sony and Microsoft directly , but you can find secondhand consoles at a variety of other retailers, along with places like eBay, Facebook Marketplace, and Craigslist. As usual, check your local or preferred retailer to see the latest prices.

New and certified refurbished consoles come with everything you need--including the system, controller, and power cords. You will need a TV or monitor, but the odds are good that if you're looking to play GTA 6, you probably already have one.

People on platforms outside PlayStation and Xbox are out of luck, as GTA 6 has not been announced for Switch 2 or PC. A PC edition is expected to release in early 2027 , but there is no word on a Switch 2 version.
The game

To play GTA 6 you will need to buy GTA 6. The game's standard edition goes for $80, with its Ultimate Edition selling for $100. As mentioned, the game is not available on a disc. That being said, retailers are selling the $80 edition in stores, though you only get a code in the box. The $100 edition appears to be exclusive to digital storefronts.

The $100 Ultimate Edition includes loads of extras , including a variety of cosmetics and even in-game shops that people who buy the $80 edition cannot access. Since GTA 6 is a digital-exclusive game, there is no reason to worry about units selling out, but if you do want to preorder, you get the Vintage Vice City Pack and a free month of GTA+.
GTA 5 launched at $60 back in 2013--adjusted for inflation, that's about $85 today.

You will also need an internet connection to install GTA 6, since it's a digital only game. It's a beefy one, too, weighing in at a reported 201GB . Thankfully, preloading begins on November 12 , a full week before the game launches. That means you'll be able to begin downloading it early in the hopes of being ready to go on November 19.

November 12 is also when GTA 6's code-in-a-box copies will be available to buy at physical stores. You're not getting a week of early access, though, as the game does not unlock fully until November 19.
Do you need PS Plus or Game Pass?
GTA 6 is a strictly single-player game, and as such, you likely will not need PlayStation Plus or Xbox Game Pass to play. Rockstar has yet to confirm this, however.

Rockstar is surely going to release a new version of GTA Online at some point-- some believe that will happen in early 2027 . And at that point, you'll likely need a membership. But for launch, there is no online or multiplayer support, so we don't think a subscription to PS Plus or Game Pass would be required.
Why no disc?

Neither Rockstar nor studio owner Take-Two have provided a reason for GTA 6 being a digital exclusive, but the answer seems pretty obvious: It's all about money. Rockstar makes more money from digital game sales, and having no disc eliminates the secondhand market.
“A disc can be resold or rented a hundred times, and Rockstar earns nothing after that first sale," Rhys Elliott of Alinea Analytics said.
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Jason_and_Lucia_02.jpg?w=636

The code-in-a-box strategy for physical games has been around for a long time already , and while people might complain online about the lack of a physical edition of GTA 6, the game is going to sell phenomenally no matter what, Mat Piscatella of Circana says.

Beyond these factors, consumer spending patterns have trended increasingly toward digital since the early 2010s. GTA 6 is such a large game in terms of its file size , so making it digital-exclusive also saves Rockstar and Take-Two money by not needing to print a second disc , if one was ever needed.
